excerpts.panel_design: 3D MERFISH (Tasks 2 and 3) Samples were profiled by 3D MERFISH on a Vizgen MERSCOPE using a 500-gene panel designed to cover all cardiac-related cell types and the cell types around them. The same panel was used at every stage and in both the heart and embryo settings. Two genes, Casp4 and Pnliprp1 , are absent from the E6.75 and E7.25 files, which is why the embryo boards carry 498 genes rather than 500. The panel itself is unchanged: both genes are expressed too lowly to be detected at those two stages.
excerpts.section_selection: 3D MERFISH sections For E7.75 and E8.0, only the sections spanning from the yolk sac–embryo boundary to the level where the cardiac crescent was no longer visible were included. For E8.25 to E9.5, only the portion of the embryo containing the heart tube was sectioned, and the yolk sac was retained. For E10.5 and E12.5, the hearts were dissected directly from the embryos and the entire heart was sectioned. There is no machine-readable region-of-interest or mask definition for the MERFISH data. Selection was made at collection, as above.
excerpts.segmentation_and_normalization: Segmentation and processing Cells were segmented from the nuclear DAPI signal with Cellpose 2. Decoded RNA molecules were then partitioned into individual cells to build single-cell count matrices. MERFISH cells with fewer than five unique genes were excluded from downstream analysis, and the remaining cells were processed with the standard Scanpy workflow. Expression in the released files is log-normalised: counts are divided by the total counts per cell, scaled to 10,000, and log1p-transformed. We checked this on every released MERFISH file: undoing the log1p gives per-cell totals of 10,000.
excerpts.annotation: Cell-type annotation Cell types were annotated by clustering followed by manual naming, carried out by Yifan Lu, stage by stage. This was a choice, not an oversight: over a time window this wide, one annotation of the merged dataset cannot resolve fine-grained cell types and states, so each stage was annotated on its own to get the finer resolution. The cost is that the vocabulary is not harmonised across stages. In the Multiome files, ventricular cardiomyocytes appear as LV-CM and RV-CM at E8.5 and are merged into V-CM at E9.5; endocardium is a single Endocardium at E9.5 and is split at later stages. A label missing from one stage may therefore be present under a different name rather than biologically absent, and comparing label sets across stages overstates how much has changed. The two assays were annotated independently and report different numbers of cell types at the same stage: 33 and 22 for MERFISH at E8.5 and E9.5, against 18 and 21 for Multiome.
